look_here_first: LOOK HERE FIRST: slimspike windmillgrass has a radiating, windmill-like head with long, very slender spikelet-bearing racemes. The existing hand photo shows individual branches, not a measured spikelet or verified awn. Start with the entire flowering head and THEN check mature fertile and sterile florets against a local Chloris key; a windmill silhouette alone does not prove the species.

comparisons.key_distinctions: Slimspike's fine elongated radiating racemes may resemble hybrid and tumble windmillgrass. The tiering of racemes, leaf/crown and mature upper sterile lemma plus fertile/sterile awns must be examined; a head that merely resembles a windmill is not sufficient. Hooded windmillgrass has short crowded branches and an inflated sterile lemma. Feather fingergrass makes a more compact terminal fan and often an annual plant.

crew_field_walkthrough: Find the central point where slender fingerlike racemes radiate; the hand photo gives an approximate scale.
Trace one branch toward its tip and note spikelet rows along its length; this broad structure does not expose lemma/awn measurements.
Get the rooted crown, several mature whole heads, and one isolated spikelet at millimeter scale before distinguishing this from shortspike hybrid or tumble windmillgrass.
what_to_photograph_for_confirmation: Whole rooted plant, lower nodes and complete mature radiating head.
Two or more full heads against ruler to compare raceme length and tiering.
Mature spikelet macro dissected to show fertile lemma and upper sterile lemma, glumes and separately measured awns.
Paired verified C. verticillata and hybrid spikelet for real species-level exclusion.

visual_comparison.subtitle: Actual installed photographs checked for visible structures; an image of a different species is explicitly labeled look-alike. Do not mislabel a whole raceme as a microscopic lemma.

items.label: 1 · Long slim radiating racemes
items.image_role: Slender branches radiate from central flowering head over a hand
items.caption: Fine racemes emerge from a central junction and radiate toward the frame edges. Source observation calls this slimspike windmillgrass. No glumes, lemma or awn are resolved well enough to certify species.
items.why_it_matters: Introduces the slender windmill shape and the correct next anatomical target.

items.photo_status: Existing exact-source physical image visually examined on 2026-10-20; arrows point only at structures that are visible. Source photograph taxon ID not independently voucher-verified; license/credit retained, public gate separately required.

items.label: LOOK-ALIKE — Chloris verticillata (different species)
items.caption: The compared photograph belongs to Chloris verticillata, not Chloris andropogonoides. Notice overlapping windmill forms, then confirm identity with the unpictured sterile lemma and awn anatomy.
items.why_it_matters: Shows why broad seedhead shape alone often cannot prove the exact species.
